subject: Post-call: reranker integration / top_k evaluation & architecture questions
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finserv.io>; Product Team <product@finserv.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps: reranker / top_k evaluation & infra notes

Hi Elena / FinServ team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Short recap and concrete next steps so we all have the same plan: 

TL;DR: FinServ wants to evaluate a reranker-based ranking pipeline for transaction search relevance. We agreed Redwood will provide a short POC-grade integration (SDK + small eval harness) focusing on: top_k tuning, latency/throughput targets, and relevance metrics for QA.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary goal: Improve precision@5 and reduce noisy results for entity search across transaction descriptions.
- Success metrics: lift in MAP@10 or nDCG (we flagged MAP and nDCG as candidates), baseline will be your internal sampling set.
- Latency targets: 95th percentile < 200ms for reranker calls in the POC (combined encode + rank).
- Traffic: initial POC will be batched offline (10k queries) then a limited online trial (peak ~25 qps).

Action items (owners / ETA):
1) Redwood: provide SDK snippets (Python + Node) for embedding + ranking APIs, plus an example for top_k sweep. Deliverable: small repo + integration doc. (Owner: vanessa / marcus) — ETA 2027-04-06.
2) FinServ: share a 500–1k sample of queries + labeled relevancy judgments or a seed annotation spreadsheet. (Owner: Elena) — ETA 2027-04-07.
3) Redwood engineering: propose an architecture for hybrid routing (embedding store + online reranker) and latency profile. (Owner: marcus) — ETA 2027-04-05.
4) Both: agree on evaluation metrics (MAP@K, nDCG, precision@K) and top_k grid for sweep (K candidates: 1,3,5,10). Meeting to finalize: Calendly link below.

Attachments: FS-reranker-eval-seed_prompts.csv (placeholder sample), MVP-integration-map.pdf (sketch of data flow), reranker-qps-estimates.xlsx (back-of-envelope QPS/latency).

Notes on architecture points we discussed (high level):
- Auth: token-based with short-lived keys (we'll provide instructions for scoped API keys for the POC).
- SDK: client will fetch embeddings from Redwood and call ranking endpoint with candidate set; we support both passing in precomputed embeddings and raw text for server-side encoding.
- Routing/fallback: we can route to a cheaper dense-only model if reranker capacity is saturated; will provide routing policy suggestions.
- Structured output/tool-calling: not part of the initial POC, but built-in if you want structured provenance metadata returned per-scored item.

Next step: Marcus will send an architecture note and the SDK snippets by Mon (Apr 5). Vanessa will post the HubSpot activity and the Drive folder with the sample artifacts.

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Vanessa Ortiz

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finserv.io>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call recap + next steps: reranker / top_k evaluation & infra notes

Vanessa — quick note with the architecture sketch I promised. I attached more detail to the Drive link Vanessa shared. High-level notes: 

1) Candidate generation: client-side or service-side; for the POC we'll assume FinServ will provide candidate IDs per query (top 100 from a sparse search). That keeps the POC simple and focuses on reranker quality.

2) Embeddings vs server encoding:
   - If you precompute embeddings for the candidate pool and send them with the request, reranker latency drops ~30–50ms because we avoid encode on each candidate.
   - If you send raw text and let Redwood encode server-side, the system is simpler but adds per-candidate encode cost; acceptable for offline/batch evaluation.

3) Ranking API pattern (recommended):
   POST /v1/ranker/score
   body: { query_embedding: [...], candidates: [{id, embedding? | text, metadata}], top_k: 1..K, return_metadata: true }

   Response: array of scored candidates with scores, normalized relevance, and a trace-id for correlating logs.

4) Top_k tuning plan:
   - Sweep K in [1,3,5,10] using MAP@10 and nDCG as primary metrics. Also track precision@1 and precision@5.
   - Use bootstrap sampling on your labeled set for confidence intervals.

5) Latency optimizations:
   - Batch candidate encoding when possible.
   - Use cached embeddings (prefix/KV cache) for frequently used candidate docs.
   - If online qps > 50, consider dedicated pools. For POC (~25 qps) shared infra is fine.

6) Observability: We'll emit per-request timing (encode, scoring, serialization) and token-level cost so we can correlate quality vs cost.

Open questions for FinServ: 
- Do you have a regularly updated candidate index we can attach IDs to, or will the candidate list be ad-hoc per query?
- What relevance labels do you have available (binary relevance, graded scales 0-3)? Graded labels enable nDCG easily.

I'll drop example SDK snippets into the Drive folder tonight (python + node).

--
Marcus Lin
Backend Engineer, Runtime Integrations | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finserv.io>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Product Team <product@finserv.io>
Date: 2027-04-04T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps: reranker / top_k evaluation & infra notes

Thanks Vanessa & Marcus — that looks good and matches our internal thoughts. A few clarifications & answers below.

1) Candidate index: we maintain a nightly updated candidate set (IDs + text + metadata). We can export the top-100 per query for the POC.

2) Labels: we have a graded relevance pool labeled 0/1/2 (2 = exact match, 1 = partial) for about 2,400 hand-labeled queries. We'll export a 1k sample for the initial evaluation and keep the rest for later.

3) Latency: for the online trial we can tolerate up to 250ms p95 initially. We noted 200ms in the meeting — 250ms is acceptable for our first live run.

4) Auth & security: we'll want scoped API keys for the POC. Can you confirm short-lived tokens are supported and whether we can restrict them by IP?

5) Attachments: we'll upload the 1k sample + label schema to the Drive folder by EOD tomorrow.

Open question from our side:
- In your ranking API, do you expose a normalized score across model variants so we can compare different reranker models without re-scaling? That would help with A/B comparisons.

Happy to sync over a short call tomorrow if that helps — scheduling link please.

Best,
Elena
Senior Product Manager | FinServ Analytics
elena.rossi@finserv.io

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finserv.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call recap + next steps: reranker / top_k evaluation & infra notes

Perfect — thanks for the quick responses, Elena. Short replies inline: 

- Candidate export: great, send the 1k sample and we'll begin the MAP/nDCG runs.
- Labels: 0/1/2 graded labels are perfect for nDCG. We'll include evaluation code to compute both MAP@10 and nDCG@10.
- Latency: noted p95 target 250ms for online trial; we'll aim for <200ms in the POC but accept 250ms for initial rollout.
- Auth/IP restrictions: we support short-lived scoped API keys. IP restrictions are not available on self-serve keys today, but for the Private/Dedicated options we can add IP allowlists. For the POC we can issue scoped keys and rotate them via the Drive instructions.
- Normalized scores: yes — Redwood returns both raw model logits and a normalized 0-1 relevance score (model-specific but normalized per-run). We'll document that in the SDK.

Next steps summary:
- Vanessa/Marcus: push SDK snippets + ranking API example + evaluation harness to Drive by EOD today.
- Elena: upload the 1k labeled sample by EOD tomorrow (2027-04-06).
- Schedule: On Wed (2027-04-07) we'll run the first sweep and share results by Fri (2027-04-09).

Scheduling: https://calendly.com/vanessa-redwood/30min (please pick a slot if you want a quick sync).

I'll also log this in HubSpot and attach the Drive folder.

Thanks — excited to get this running.
